summary.title: Summary
summary.formWarning: No valid fields — please review the “Form” step.

form.p1: Define the fields applicants fill in when submitting.
form.p2: The field key identifies a field technically and serves as the variable name in the flow; it must be unique per form.
form.p3: Labels are multilingual: German, French, Italian and English are required for publishing.
form.p4: Save as draft at any time — the request type only goes live in the “Publish” step.

flow.p1: Model the workflow as a graph: start, form, approval, action, branch (XOR), parallel (AND) and end.
flow.p2: Add nodes from the palette on the left; drag edges from a node's right-hand output to the next node's left-hand input.
flow.p3: Outgoing XOR edges take conditions of the form variable == 'value' (or !=); the variable is a field key or an approval outcome.
flow.p4: Exactly one XOR edge stays without a condition — it is the default path when no condition matches.
flow.p5: Warnings in the inspector on the right show open issues; the server fully validates the graph on publish.

publish.p1: The summary shows fields, nodes and edges plus the draft's save state.
publish.p2: On publish the server fully validates the graph (start/end, reachability, XOR conditions) and requires the title and labels in all four languages.
publish.p3: Publishing puts the version LIVE: applicants can submit requests immediately; exactly one version is live per request type.
publish.p4: Unsaved valid changes are saved automatically before publishing.

help.title: Help center
help.lead: Step-by-step guides and guided tours for HR-Suite.

designer.title: HR designer: create and publish a request type
designer.step1: Open “Request types” and create the key and the title in all four languages via “New request type”.
designer.step2: Define the fields in the builder's “Form” step; each field needs a unique key.
designer.step3: Maintain the field labels in German, French, Italian and English — without complete translations the server rejects publishing.
designer.step4: Model the workflow in the “Flow” step: place the start node, add steps (form, approval, action), connect edges by dragging, place the end node.
designer.step5: Add conditions to XOR outputs in the form variable == 'value' (or !=); exactly one edge stays unconditioned as the default path.
designer.step6: Save as draft and check the summary in the “Publish” step.
designer.step7: Publish: the version goes LIVE and the workflow is deployed as a process.

applicant.title: Applicants: submit and track a request
applicant.step2: Select a published request type; the form appears automatically.
applicant.step3: Fill in the fields and submit with “Create & submit”.
applicant.step4: Track the status of your request in the list (e.g. Submitted, Completed).
applicant.step5: You can submit or cancel drafts later.

reviewer.title: Reviewers: check tasks and decide
reviewer.step1: Open “Tasks” — the open review tasks are listed there.
reviewer.step2: Open a task's request data via “Details”.
reviewer.step4: Decide with “Approve” or “Reject” — or complete the task.
reviewer.step5: The request then automatically receives the new status.
